classes.name: Warrior
classes.description: A durable, hard-hitting frontline fighter who uses Rage, stances and weapon mastery.
strengths: Can serve as either a tank or damage dealer.
Strong sustained damage against multiple melee targets.
Brings class-specific group buffs and debuffs.
limitations: Has limited tools for recovering after taking heavy damage.
soloTips: Plan recovery between difficult fights; Warriors have limited self-recovery tools.
groupUtility: Provides distinctive group buffs and debuffs.

starterGuide.reason: A two-weapon path that grows stronger as its key talents come online; the guide notes slower early progress and stresses weapon upgrades.
combat: Keep both weapon skills and weapons current; missed swings also mean less Rage.
Use Rage on the current target instead of swapping stances without a reason.
starterGuide.resource: Rage comes from combat; missed attacks can slow your next ability choices.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Keep an eye out for the class quest chain; the linked Forever leveling guide includes level-based milestones and zone/dungeon suggestions.
starterGuide.gear: The guide prioritizes current weapons; Fury depends on two maintained weapons.
beginnerMistakes: Fury is slower before key talents and strong weapons.
Frequent stance changes can complicate Rage management.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Use the Alliance or Horde zones shown for your current bracket in the linked Forever guide; its route is level-sensitive.

journeySteps.label: Level 20: train Dual Wielding and keep both weapon skills current.

levelingBands.combat: Use your best current weapon and avoid risky extra pulls while your recovery kit is limited.
levelingBands.survival: Keep weapon skill moving with your equipment upgrades.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent milestone recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: Continue with your strongest weapon; the source recommends waiting on the two-weapon Fury setup until Dual Wield is trained.
levelingBands.survival: Missed attacks mean less Rage, so weapon skill matters.
levelingBands.milestones: No level-specific point path is reproduced here.

levelingBands.combat: Train Dual Wield at 20. Fury becomes stronger as its key talents and two useful weapons come together.
levelingBands.survival: Keep both weapons current; stance swaps can make Rage management tedious.
levelingBands.milestones: Dual Wield training at level 20.

classes.name: Paladin

specializations.name: Holy
specializations.focus: Single-target healing, group support and spell-focused damage.

specializations.name: Retribution
specializations.focus: Weapon attacks blended with Holy damage.

classes.description: A versatile champion whose Seals and Judgements support melee combat, healing and protection.
strengths: Holy supports single-target healing, group support and spell-focused damage.
Protection develops threat, mana and survival tools.
Retribution blends weapon attacks with Holy damage.

starterGuide.reason: The Forever leveling guide describes Retribution as efficient, with strong single-target damage, self-healing and defensive tools.
combat: Maintain your chosen Seal and use its Judgement when it is useful.
Use healing and defensive abilities to recover from a dangerous pull.
starterGuide.resource: Healing and offensive spells share Mana; carry water and avoid spending Mana on low-risk overkill.
starterGuide.classMilestones: A Paladin weapon questline opens at level 20; Alliance and Horde receive different weapon rewards. Redemption is listed as a level-12 class quest unlock.
starterGuide.gear: Keep weapon DPS current; weapon speed influences which Seal the guide recommends.
beginnerMistakes: Limited ranged tagging and no slow are listed weaknesses.
Health can be fine while Mana is too low to heal; bring water.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: At low levels the guide lists Loch Modan/Darkshore for Alliance and The Barrens for Horde; level-sensitive options appear in the source.

journeySteps.label: Level 12: the Redemption class quest becomes available.
Level 20: begin the faction-specific class weapon questline.

levelingBands.combat: Learn the Seal and Judgement loop, and keep Mana available for healing.
levelingBands.survival: Paladin leveling has limited mobility and little ranged tagging.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent allocation recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: Use defensive tools when a pull gets dangerous; the class quest guide lists Redemption at level 12.
levelingBands.survival: Bring water so healing and combat spells do not leave you dry.
levelingBands.milestones: Lay on Hands and Blessing of Protection at 10; Redemption quest at 12.

levelingBands.combat: Begin the faction-specific weapon questline at 20; the leveling guide lists Consecration at 20 and Pursuit of Justice at 22.
levelingBands.survival: Use Consecration when multiple enemies make its cost worthwhile.
levelingBands.milestones: Faction weapon quest begins at 20; Repentance at 30.

classes.name: Hunter
classes.description: A ranged fighter supported by a loyal pet, with options built around precision, traps and melee tools.
strengths: Pets gain broader ability access, family abilities and gear scaling.
Traps can be used during combat.
soloTips: A pet-focused specialization is available; the source does not rank leveling builds.
groupUtility: Ranged damage and a combat toolkit that includes traps.

starterGuide.reason: The Forever guide describes the pet as a major leveling power increase after the level-10 pet quest, helping absorb pressure while you deal damage.
combat: Complete the level-10 pet quest promptly, send your pet first, and keep its threat in mind.
Use traps and movement tools when a pull becomes unsafe.
starterGuide.resource: Mana can run low during repeated ability use; use the pet and basic attacks to avoid needless casts.
starterGuide.classMilestones: The level-10 class quest unlocks pets and is a major power milestone. The source also lists a level-50 gear quest, not an early unlock.
starterGuide.gear: Keep your ranged weapon current; the guide recommends an early bow upgrade.
beginnerMistakes: Pet abilities/ranks require learning from suitable tamed pets.
A critical hit can pull threat from your pet; use defensive tools and bring a loose enemy toward the group tank.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Use the guide’s faction and level filters; it recommends completing useful zone quest chains before travel.

journeySteps.label: Level 10: complete the pet class quest and learn to tame a pet.
Level 20: train Aspect of the Cheetah.

levelingBands.combat: Stay at range and use your bow; the pet power spike comes after completing the level-10 class quest.
levelingBands.survival: Avoid letting several enemies reach melee range.
levelingBands.milestones: No pre-pet talent allocation listed here.

levelingBands.combat: Complete the pet quest, send the pet in first, and give it time to hold threat before your big hits.
levelingBands.survival: Your pet can tank, but it does not have unlimited multi-target threat.
levelingBands.milestones: Level 10 pet quest; Aspect of the Cheetah at 20 is the next milestone.

levelingBands.combat: Train Aspect of the Cheetah at 20; the Forever guide lists Summon Hawk as a level-25 talent unlock and Feign Death at 30.
levelingBands.survival: Use traps and threat control if an enemy peels off your pet.
levelingBands.milestones: Aspect of the Cheetah 20; Summon Hawk talent 25; Feign Death 30.

classes.name: Rogue
classes.description: A precise combatant who uses stealth, control, poisons and weapon attacks to create openings.
strengths: Forever updates expand poison use and weapon options.
Specialization paths support daggers, other weapon types, finishers, bleeds and combat tricks.

starterGuide.reason: The Forever guide centers the leveling path on reliable single-target damage and gives access to Blade Flurry for multiple enemies.
combat: Generate Combo Points with Sinister Strike, then spend them with Eviscerate.
Stealth lets you choose encounters; use it to avoid unnecessary fights.
starterGuide.resource: Energy and Combo Points are your combat loop; avoid spending finishers with too few Combo Points when the target will survive.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Check the class-quest guide for race-specific chains; no early unlock level is repeated here without verifying the player’s race.
starterGuide.gear: Keep weapons current; consult the level-sensitive guide for the priority at your level.
beginnerMistakes: The source notes limited AoE compared with other leveling classes.
Stealth helps choose fights but does not replace managing health between them.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Use the source’s level slider for faction-appropriate zones and dungeon options.

journeySteps.label: Level 20: the Combat leveling guide identifies Riposte as a major talent breakpoint.

levelingBands.combat: Use Stealth to choose encounters. Build Combo Points with Sinister Strike, then spend them with Eviscerate.
levelingBands.survival: Rogue has strong single-target damage but limited consistent AoE and self-sustain.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent milestone recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: Keep fights deliberate; use your control tools and avoid spending every defensive cooldown on routine pulls.
levelingBands.survival: The leveling source recommends choosing encounters with Stealth rather than taking every nearby mob.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent milestone recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: The Combat guide calls out Riposte at 20 as a major breakpoint; it strikes after a parry and disarms the target.
levelingBands.survival: Rogue has little self-sustain, so manage health between fights.
levelingBands.milestones: Riposte level-20 talent milestone.

classes.name: Priest
classes.description: A cloth-wearing spellcaster who supports allies with healing and buffs or turns to damaging magic.
strengths: Supports allies through buffs and healing.
Holy and Discipline include healing tools; Shadow provides a damage path.
limitations: Wears cloth armor and has few ways to escape enemies.
soloTips: Limited escape tools make positioning and avoiding unwanted enemies useful considerations.
groupUtility: Healing and buffs strengthen party members.

starterGuide.reason: The Forever guide recommends wand damage and Spirit Tap to limit Mana downtime, with shield and healing spells as safety tools.
combat: Use a small number of spells, then finish with your wand to conserve Mana.
Power Word: Shield can reduce incoming damage and spell pushback when solo.
starterGuide.resource: Mana is tight early; a current wand is a major upgrade, and Spirit Tap rewards a killing blow.
starterGuide.classMilestones: The guide lists race-specific Priest quests; consult the class quest route for the player’s race.
starterGuide.gear: Upgrade your wand regularly; the source says wand auto-attacks make a large share of early damage.
beginnerMistakes: Repeatedly casting every damage spell on every mob creates unnecessary Mana downtime.
Priest is less tanky and mobile than many classes; avoid extra pulls.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Use the linked guide’s level slider for faction-specific zone brackets and quest rewards.

journeySteps.label: Level 10: check the race-specific Priest quest route.
Level 20: check the second race-specific Priest quest route.

levelingBands.combat: A good wand matters: use a few spells, then let the wand finish the enemy to protect Mana.
levelingBands.survival: Power Word: Shield helps prevent damage and spell pushback.
levelingBands.milestones: Wand Specialization and Spirit Tap are the guide’s early talent priorities.

levelingBands.combat: Continue the wand-and-Mana rhythm; check your race-specific Priest class quest at level 10.
levelingBands.survival: Use the shield when solo enemies can interrupt your casts.
levelingBands.milestones: Race-specific Priest quest at 10; Inner Fire at 12.

levelingBands.combat: Mind Flay and Devouring Plague are listed at 20; Vampiric Embrace is a talent milestone at 25.
levelingBands.survival: The guide recommends spending only the Mana needed, then finishing with your wand.
levelingBands.milestones: Mind Flay and Devouring Plague 20; Vampiric Embrace talent 25.

classes.name: Shaman
classes.description: An adaptable elemental combatant whose totems provide buffs, healing and utility.
strengths: Can deal melee or spell damage and heal.
Mail armor and shields contribute to its sturdier class toolkit.
limitations: The official overview describes limited crowd control.
groupUtility: Totems provide buffs, healing and utility.
Can fill damage or healing roles.

starterGuide.reason: A melee path with strong burst, self-healing and Ghost Wolf mobility; its key limitation is early Mana pressure.
combat: Before level 30, use Rockbiter Weapon; apply Lightning Shield between pulls.
At level 25, Stormstrike is a major milestone; use it when ready and spend shocks deliberately.
starterGuide.resource: Auto-attacks can finish weak enemies without Mana. Spirit regeneration pauses for five seconds after spending Mana.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Call of Fire should be completed promptly for the Fire Totem; Call of Water opens at 20. Other totem quests take travel, and Call of Air requires a Razorfen Kraul run.
starterGuide.gear: Keep a slow two-handed weapon current; the guide prioritizes weapon DPS, then values Intellect for damage scaling and Mana.
beginnerMistakes: Overcasting slows your pace through drinking.
Multiple enemies can overwhelm you; use self-healing and utility rather than assuming every pull is safe.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: The source lists Alliance early routes through Loch Modan, Westfall and Darkshore; Horde through The Barrens and Silverpine. Use its live level-sensitive route.

journeySteps.label: Call of Earth: level 4 details in the source are for Dwarf Shamans; other race routes differ.
Call of Fire: pick up the Shaman quest for your Fire Totem.
Call of Water: the Water Totem quest opens at level 20.
Call of Air: the route includes a Razorfen Kraul run; exact level varies by race route.

levelingBands.combat: Use Rockbiter Weapon before level 30, keep Lightning Shield up between pulls, and let auto-attacks finish weak enemies.
levelingBands.survival: Call of Earth level-4 details in the source are specific to Dwarf Shamans.
levelingBands.milestones: Call of Earth quest route varies by race.

levelingBands.combat: Pick up Call of Fire for the Fire Totem; drop useful totems before engaging rather than spending Mana mid-fight without a reason.
levelingBands.survival: Mana is the early constraint; spending Mana pauses Spirit regeneration for five seconds.
levelingBands.milestones: Call of Fire quest; Shamanistic Focus is recommended at 20.

levelingBands.combat: Call of Water opens at 20. Stormstrike is a key level-25 build milestone; Windfury Weapon becomes available at 30.
levelingBands.survival: Use Shocks selectively and keep your weapon upgraded.
levelingBands.milestones: Shamanistic Focus 20; Stormstrike around 25; Windfury Weapon 30.

classes.name: Mage
classes.description: A fragile ranged spellcaster who chooses among Arcane, Fire and Frost tools.
strengths: Offers ranged single-target and area damage.
Polymorph provides crowd control.
Can provide party buffs and conjured food and water.
limitations: Fragile when caught in melee combat.
soloTips: Frost offers combat control; the official overview does not rank a leveling build.
groupUtility: Polymorph, party buffs, and conjured food and water.

starterGuide.reason: Forever’s Arcane tree is reworked around Arcane Blast and Missile Barrage, making it a supported leveling option rather than a generic Classic-era fallback.
combat: Build damage with Arcane Blast and use Arcane Missiles when Missile Barrage procs.
Use crowd control and range to prevent enemies from interrupting casts.
starterGuide.resource: Arcane talents improve Mana efficiency, but spell-heavy pulls still require watching your Mana and using conjured supplies.
starterGuide.classMilestones: The linked Forever guide has level-based class milestones; no separate quest unlock is asserted here.
starterGuide.gear: The source recommends keeping crafting gear in mind; specific stat priorities should follow the current guide.
beginnerMistakes: Standing still to cast can be risky when enemies reach you.
Do not apply Retail or old Classic rotations to Forever’s Arcane changes.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: The source provides level-sensitive zone and dungeon suggestions; choose the current faction and level there.

journeySteps.label: Level 20: Arcane Blast becomes available in the Forever Arcane leveling guide.
Level 25: Missile Barrage is a listed Arcane milestone.

levelingBands.combat: Play at range and avoid pulling more enemies than you can safely cast through. The Forever guide identifies Arcane as a redesigned leveling option.
levelingBands.survival: Arcane is a caster path; bad proc luck or gear can increase downtime.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent allocation is recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: Use the spells you have trained and conserve Mana between pulls; do not import a Retail or other Classic rotation.
levelingBands.survival: Arcane’s Forever changes make its own leveling guide the relevant reference.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent milestone recorded before the new Arcane core.

levelingBands.combat: Arcane Blast is listed at 20 and Missile Barrage at 25; use Arcane Missiles when the proc empowers it.
levelingBands.survival: Arcane’s resource talents help sustain, but watch Mana during repeated casts.
levelingBands.milestones: Arcane Blast 20; Missile Barrage 25; Arcane Explosion 14.

classes.name: Warlock
classes.description: A spellcaster who combines Shadow and Fire magic with demonic allies.
strengths: Forever specializations support damage-over-time, demon synergies, and Shadow/Fire combinations.
Pets scale with their master’s stats.
limitations: Physically weak and relies on demon pets for protection.
soloTips: Demon pets can help protect the Warlock; no comparative leveling ranking is published here.

starterGuide.reason: A damage-over-time playstyle with a demon, drains and Life Tap; the Forever guide emphasizes planning health and Mana together.
combat: Use your demon deliberately: Voidwalker offers safer solo pulls; keep pet commands easy to reach.
Apply damage-over-time spells, then use direct damage or drains as the situation allows.
starterGuide.resource: Life Tap converts health into Mana; use Drain Life, food and bandages to manage the health cost.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Warlock class quests involve travel and demon unlocks; pick up the chain before leaving town and consult the class quest guide for exact race/level steps.
starterGuide.gear: The leveling guide values Spell Power and Shadow damage for its main spells; choose current upgrades rather than a fixed item list.
beginnerMistakes: Life Tap at low health can leave you vulnerable.
Keep demon Grimoires trained; pet ability ranks are handled separately.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Collect flight paths and combine class-quest travel with nearby zone and trainer stops.

journeySteps.label: Level 6: train Life Tap; balance its health cost with recovery.
Level 20: Rain of Fire adds a ranged area-damage option.

levelingBands.combat: Life Tap is learned at 6; trade health for Mana carefully and use Drain Life or recovery between fights.
levelingBands.survival: Keep an eye on Health before using Life Tap again.
levelingBands.milestones: Life Tap 6; Immolate is available from level 1.

levelingBands.combat: Use your demon and damage-over-time spells to manage pressure; train spell ranks and demon abilities at trainers.
levelingBands.survival: Use Life Tap with recovery in mind, not as free Mana.
levelingBands.milestones: Drain Life 14; guide lists Corruption ranks beginning at 4 and Shadow Bolt ranks at 1.

levelingBands.combat: Rain of Fire is listed at 20; Shadow Bolt can gain instant-cast Nightfall procs from 25 in the guide’s build.
levelingBands.survival: Area casts can spend resources quickly; avoid adding enemies just because an AoE spell is available.
levelingBands.milestones: Rain of Fire 20; Nightfall talent procs from 25; Firestone is listed from 28.

classes.name: Druid
classes.description: A nature-focused class with adaptable forms and distinct spellcasting, melee and healing paths.
strengths: Feral supports form-based melee and tanking approaches.
Balance provides a spellcasting damage path.
Restoration focuses on healing.
groupUtility: Can approach combat through damage, tanking or healing paths.

starterGuide.reason: The Forever guide highlights Feral’s flexibility between damage and tanking, mobility and self-healing. Bear and Cat forms arrive at levels 10 and 20.
combat: Use the form suited to the task: Bear for durability, Cat for melee damage once available.
Expect a slower opening before the form unlocks; use healing tools between fights.
starterGuide.resource: Shifting and healing have costs; avoid unnecessary form changes and keep recovery between pulls in mind.
starterGuide.classMilestones: Form unlocks are major class milestones; the linked class-quest guide has race-specific quest steps.
starterGuide.gear: Follow the source’s level-sensitive priorities; no single weapon/stat rule is assumed for all forms.
beginnerMistakes: Feral’s full leveling rhythm changes at levels 10 and 20 as forms unlock.
Do not treat Bear and Cat as identical roles.
starterGuide.zoneAdvice: Use the source’s live faction and level route; the linked guide includes Forever-specific dungeon and zone recommendations.

levelingBands.combat: Feral’s leveling pace improves after its forms unlock; use the class kit and avoid assuming the later Cat/Bear rhythm is already available.
levelingBands.survival: The guide calls the pre-form stretch slower than later leveling.
levelingBands.milestones: No exact talent allocation recorded for this band.

levelingBands.combat: Bear Form becomes available at 10, adding the path’s tank-oriented form option.
levelingBands.survival: Use the form that fits the pull rather than treating every fight as Cat play.
levelingBands.milestones: Bear Form level 10.

levelingBands.combat: Cat Form becomes available at 20; the Forever guide highlights Feral’s mobility and ability to shift between damage and tank roles.
levelingBands.survival: The guide notes Cat Form has no AoE damage.
levelingBands.milestones: Cat Form level 20.

zones.name: Mount Hyjal
zones.access: Story access details not yet documented

specialAccess: Skyborne characters and the Zephras Isle starting experience require the Heroic Pack or higher.
classNotes: Specialization roles and Forever identities are drawn from linked Blizzard deep-dives. Enhancement Shaman also has a dedicated, current Forever leveling and combat guide. Other class pages remain concise reference pages until class-specific play guides are researched.
buildProfileNote: No complete, version-verified talent loadouts have been published in this guide yet. Use specialization pages as sourced class overviews; do not treat them as point-by-point builds.

strengths: High single-target burst once the core talents come online.
Strong area damage becomes available early.
Self-healing helps recover after difficult pulls.
Ghost Wolf supports travel; the leveling guide calls out improved mobility after level 20.
weaknesses: Mana is a frequent constraint, especially before sustain talents.
Weapon upgrades matter greatly to melee damage.
The opening levels can feel slower before Stormstrike.
Several enemies at once can overwhelm the build.

talentMilestones.name: Shamanistic Focus
talentMilestones.note: The leveling guide calls this out for reducing Shock mana costs; it does not publish a rank in the text.

talentMilestones.name: Stormstrike
talentMilestones.note: The guide recommends reaching the Enhancement core around this point and describes an optional respec at 25.

talentMilestones.name: Improved Stormstrike
talentMilestones.note: The guide marks this as a Mana-sustain and cooldown-reset pickup; it does not publish a rank in the text.

talentMilestones.name: Windfury Weapon
talentMilestones.note: The leveling guide identifies this as a major power spike at level 30; use Rockbiter Weapon before then.

talentMilestones.name: Mindfulness
talentMilestones.note: The leveling guide recommends returning to Restoration for additional passive Mana sustain.

talentMilestones.name: Water Shield
talentMilestones.note: The guide lists this as a further Mana return option.

levelingRotation.title: Keep ready
items: Before level 30, use Rockbiter Weapon; from level 30, the leveling guide recommends Windfury Weapon.
Place only the totems useful for the next fight; totems stay where placed.

levelingRotation.title: During a pull
items: Use a low-rank Lightning Bolt to pull a distant enemy when helpful.
Use Stormstrike on cooldown once learned; respond to Improved Stormstrike resets once talented.
Use Earth Shock for damage or to interrupt a spellcaster.
Use Flame Shock on multiple enemies; use Frost Shock when threat is a concern.
Use Fire Nova when a Fire Totem is active and Mana allows; otherwise keep attacking.
Heal with Healing Wave after a pull and drink when Mana is low.

singleTargetRotation: Keep Magma Totem active; use Searing Totem when Mana is tight.
Use Rage of the Farseer when talented, for priority targets or a planned burst window.
Use Stormstrike on its six-second cycle.
Cast Lightning Bolt when Maelstrom Weapon reaches five stacks; avoid spending fewer stacks because it can reset the swing timer.
Use Earth Shock; use Fire Nova with a Fire Totem active when Mana permits.
aoeRotation: Keep a Fire Totem active and use Fire Nova on its cycle.
Use Rage of the Farseer when talented.
Use Stormstrike and Earth Shock between Fire Nova casts.
Spend Maelstrom Weapon at five stacks when talented.
AoE is Mana intensive; reduce optional casts when resources run low.
precombat: Use the recommended weapon imbue for your level/build.
For a group, the guide lists Strength of Earth, a Fire Totem, Mana Spring, and Windfury Totem as the baseline set; trade Magma for Searing if Mana is limited.
utility: Strength of Earth Totem for group Strength; Stoneskin Totem when physical defense matters.
Windfury Totem for groups; Grounding Totem against spellcasters.
Earthbind Totem for slowing nearby threats; Tremor Totem for Fear, Charm, and Sleep.
Totemic Recall can recover Mana when moving and replacing totems.
Healing Wave for efficient recovery between pulls.
levelingStats: Weapon DPS first; prefer a slow two-handed weapon (the guide suggests approximately 3.3–3.8 speed).
Intellect for Mana and talent scaling.
Strength for melee damage, especially before Intellect scaling improves.
Spirit becomes more useful for Mana sustain after Improved Stormstrike or Mindfulness.
Agility and Stamina are situational secondary choices.
endgameStats: Weapon DPS, Hit Chance, Expertise, Intellect, Strength, then Spell Power.

quests.name: Call of Earth
quests.reward: Earth Totem; the Dwarf route also lists Stoneskin Totem.
quests.note: The level 4 details cited are for Dwarf Shaman; other race routes differ.

quests.name: Call of Fire
quests.reward: Fire Totem; the Dwarf route lists Searing Totem.
quests.note: Icy Veins says this can be picked up from any Shaman Trainer.

quests.name: Call of Water
quests.note: The guide recommends fitting this longer travel chain between other quests.

quests.name: Call of Air
quests.note: The leveling guide says this involves a Razorfen Kraul run and travel through multiple zones; race-specific details vary.

level60Builds.name: Standard Level 60 PvE
level60Builds.summary: Stormstrike and Improved Stormstrike form the core; the source also recommends Maelstrom Weapon, Rage of the Farseer, and Elemental picks including Elemental Devastation and Trial by Fire. Improved Ghost Wolf is optional; the source suggests two Tidal Focus points if skipped.
alternatives: Windfury Weapon is the source’s default imbue. Rockbiter may be preferable if Totem mechanics favor it; this remains unresolved in the source.
A Flametongue dagger setup is described as a possibility, not a verified recommendation.

level60Builds.name: Solo and small-group Level 60
level60Builds.summary: Trades deep Enhancement talents Maelstrom Weapon and Rage of the Farseer for more Mana sustain through Mindfulness while retaining Trial by Fire.
alternatives: The source frames this as an option when Judgement of Wisdom support is unreliable and Mana is a problem.
